plans.note: Section 15 is headed 'Limitation of Garman's Liability', suggesting a one-way cap; check amount, mutuality and carve-outs (IP indemnity in sec-13, confidentiality in sec-14, willful misconduct).

Section 13 is the IP indemnity from Garman; assess scope (defend/indemnify, remedies, exclusions) and whether any reciprocal customer indemnity is broader than narrow; check sec-15 for indemnity carve-out from the cap.

No non-compete heading; a software licence of this type rarely restricts our business lines. Sweep sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) and sec-20 (General Matters) for any restraint on competing products before concluding absent.
No exclusivity heading; check the grant (sec-2), use restrictions (sec-3) and maintenance/fees (sec-10, sec-11) for any sole-source or exclusive-supplier language.
Pricing sits in sec-11 (Fees) and sec-10 (maintenance charges); look for any 'most favoured' or best-terms wording. Only flag if the MFN runs against us.

Section 19 is the non-solicitation clause; test mutuality, duration, scope (employees involved in the project only) and a general-advertising/unsolicited-applicant carve-out. Check sec-18 for survival period.

Section 17 governs term and termination; confirm we have convenience termination on notice without penalty (including of maintenance in sec-10) and that Garman cannot terminate mid-term at will. Sections 7-8 give a rejection/exit right at acceptance stage.

Maintenance term/renewal is likely in sec-10 with fee uplift mechanics in sec-11; check auto-renewal length, notice window for non-renewal and any price-increase cap (uplift cap is a rationale note, not a standalone deviation).
Governing law, venue and any arbitration/dispute clause will sit in sec-20 (General Matters); a Canadian/other non-listed law or foreign arbitration seat is the deviation trigger.

Assignment/change-of-control language is typically in sec-20; confirm we can assign to affiliates and successors without consent and that Garman cannot terminate on our change of control (cross-check sec-17 termination triggers and sec-2 for licence transferability).

Ownership statements likely in sec-2/sec-3 (Garman retains software IP, which is acceptable); the concern is any grant to Garman of our data, converted data (sec-4) or feedback/modifications — check sec-14 confidentiality and sec-16 escrow for our data rights.

Section 2 is the grant; test whether it is perpetual/irrevocable, extends to affiliates, authorized locations (defined in sec-1) and contractors/outsourcers, and whether sec-3 restrictions cut across those needs.

No audit heading; licence-compliance audit rights, if any, would be tucked into sec-3 (Restrictions on Use) or sec-20. If present, check notice, frequency, business hours and Garman bearing its own costs.

Look for late-payment interest, penalty or liquidated damages payable by us in sec-11 (Fees) and termination charges in sec-17; service credits or delay damages running in our favour are not to be flagged.

Section 12 (Specifications and Warranty) is primary; assess warranty duration from acceptance (sec-6), the remedy (repair/replace/refund, with sec-7/8 rejection rights) and any disclaimer of implied warranties.
No insurance heading; Garman personnel will be on site for delivery/installation (sec-4) and implementation (sec-9), so an insurance covenant is expected — check sec-20 before recording as missing.
Check sec-11 and sec-10 for minimum licence counts, committed maintenance years or take-or-pay volumes, and sec-2 for any obligation to license additional seats/locations.

Section 17 likely covers post-termination effects (return/destruction of software) and sec-18 survival; look for return of our data and migration assistance, with sec-16 escrow as a partial continuity substitute. Flag as missing only if no data-return or exit-help obligation appears.
